prompt: For days, Felix avoids the task 'sort out the trip' on his list, though each part (checking dates, comparing two options, messaging his friend) is easy. What is the most likely cause and fix?

options.text: He is lazy; the fix is to feel worse about it
The task is undefined, so his brain cannot start it; the fix is to replace it with the single next physical action and do that
The fix is to add more tasks to the list for pressure
Easy parts mean the whole task should take no planning at all

explanation: Vague tasks stall because there is no obvious first move. Defining the next concrete action — 'open the calendar and check two dates' — converts avoidance into a startable step.
